item.title: Gambit 1.3.1
item.description:
# Gambit 1.3.1
Released November 22, 2026.
## Your Mac goes on serving after a relaunch
The remote screen had one hole in it, and it was the one that made the whole feature look broken: quit Gambit, open it again, and the phone could no longer reach your Mac.
Nothing was wrong with the pairing — it was still there, in the keychain, from months ago. What was missing was a listener. A pairing survives a quit; a socket does not, and only the act of *pairing* had ever started one. So a Mac that had been paired for weeks came back from every relaunch with nothing answering, and the phone sat on "Connecting to your Mac…" to a computer open in front of you.
**It now serves itself.** A Mac with a pairing starts listening as it opens, with no code to scan and nothing to press — the address the phone already has just answers again. If the network is not up yet when Gambit opens, it tries again at ten seconds, thirty, and a minute rather than going quiet until you open Settings.
Settings › Cloud now says which it is: **Listening**, with the address your phone dials, or what stopped it. That row exists because the failure was invisible before — "paired" and "reachable" turned out to be two different facts, and the app only ever showed you the first.
Signing out of Tailscale stops the listener with the node, so the card cannot go on claiming to listen for a Mac that no longer has a name.
## A turn from your phone now acts
Asking the phone to "open YouTube" used to come back with *Browser control is off — turn on Control in the agent composer* — a switch that lives on the Mac, in a chip the phone cannot reach.
A turn started from the phone now carries its own permission, separate from the chip you set for your own typing. Pairing is the grant: the phone can act, without you having to leave a switch on for your own turns. Your Control chip still means exactly what it meant for the turns you start yourself.
## The remote feed shows a new tab
Opening a new tab on the Mac and looking at the phone showed "Connecting…" forever. A new tab has no page yet — Gambit draws the board instead — so there was nothing to photograph, and what the phone got was an empty picture that looked like a broken connection.
The board is now drawn off screen and sent, a frame every second and a half or so. Mostly it is still, so it costs almost nothing.
## Your Mac's address heals
Rename the Mac, or let Tailscale re-create its node, and the phone used to dial the old name forever — a pairing that worked, and reached nothing.
The phone now asks the Mac where it is. The Mac answers with a full, dialable address, and the phone follows it. A Mac that has been renamed is found again without pairing a second time.
## A long address stays in its pill
On the iPhone, a long address — a search, a long path — drew the field past the edge of the screen: 514 points of pill in a 402-point screen, starting off the left edge. Collapsed, the pill is now sized by the room it has rather than by how many characters it holds, so it can never be wider than the dock, at any text size.
## Also in this release
- **Remote turns respect a setting change mid-run.** Flipping Control while a turn from the phone is running cannot widen what that turn is allowed to do.
---
Your passkeys still do not work: this build's provisioning profile is missing the Web Browser entitlement, so WebAuthn is unavailable. It is unchanged from 1.3.0 and is being fixed separately.
